sections.title: Define when the backup takes over.
paragraphs: Revo’s Services page describes configurable answering timing, including answering after a few rings or during selected hours. Confirm how that behavior works with your phone provider and supported setup; no particular forwarding method is assumed.
Choose the trigger with your team: unanswered ringing, a busy line or a planned period of limited coverage. Overflow differs from after-hours coverage because the office remains open.
items: Record the normal office hours and primary answering route.
Agree when backup should answer and how callers are greeted.
Check how the phone setup handles busy and unanswered calls.

sections.title: Keep the backup message consistent with the office.
paragraphs: The caller should know whether they are leaving a service request, receiving confirmed scheduling information or waiting for a callback. Do not promise immediate access to a staff member just because the office is open.

For example, while the receptionist is assisting another customer, the backup can collect the requested service, property ZIP code and callback details under your approved policy. This is an illustrative intake scenario, not a measured reduction in missed calls.

sections.title: Assign ownership of the return to your team.
paragraphs: Decide who reviews overflow requests during the day, where that person checks them and how unresolved requests are tracked. A call summary is useful only if someone owns its next step.

Team transfers are excluded from Solo and included in Crew and Fleet in the shared official pricing data. A transfer entitlement does not establish that a person will answer; review the unavailable-person fallback.
items: Avoid creating a second request when the caller contacts the office again.
Keep existing appointments separate from new service inquiries.
Use an approved callback window your staffing can support.

sections.title: Test the busy-period transition.
paragraphs: Review a call while the office is already on another line, a call that the office answers before the backup trigger and a request that cannot be transferred. Confirm who handles each outcome.
Track handled requests and actual follow-up using your own records. Do not assume every overflow call is a qualified job or that backup coverage guarantees revenue.

faqs.q: Is overflow answering the same as after-hours answering?
faqs.a: No. Overflow backs up an open office when staff are busy. After-hours coverage follows the closed-office policy.

faqs.q: How many rings should pass before backup answers?
faqs.a: Choose a timing rule with your team and confirm that your phone provider and answering setup support it. This guide does not prescribe a universal ring count.

faqs.q: Can every plan transfer an overflow call to staff?
faqs.a: The shared official pricing data excludes transfers from Solo and includes them in Crew and Fleet. Confirm the supported setup and fallback before using transfers.

record.takeaway: Keep a busy office from becoming an unclear next step.

record.description: A remodeling answering service helps capture every project inquiry, appointment request, and update call, so you never miss an opportunity.
record.lead: A remodeling answering service can handle calls that start with a kitchen idea, a bathroom project inquiry, or a question about ongoing work. While you’re meeting clients or working on-site, the service collects the details your office needs, so you stay connected to every opportunity and keep projects moving smoothly.
record.intro:
A remodeling answering service can handle calls that start with a kitchen idea, a bathroom project inquiry, or a question about ongoing work. While you’re meeting clients or working on-site, the service collects the details your office needs, so you stay connected to every opportunity and keep projects moving smoothly.

Separate the sales conversation from project administration at intake. New inquiries need scope and planning context; existing customers need their question connected to the right project and authorized person. Neither should leave the call with an unapproved commitment.

sections.title: A homeowner is exploring a remodel
paragraphs: Capture the rooms or work involved, property location and stage of planning for a consultation review.

sections.title: A caller wants to discuss an estimate
paragraphs: Identify whether there is already a quote or visit so the office can find the relevant record.

sections.title: An existing customer requests a change
paragraphs: Record the request without accepting additional work, a revised price or a new completion date.

sections.title: Information to collect
items: Rooms or project scope described by the caller
Preferred consultation period and follow-up owner

sections.title: Give each request a defined next step
paragraphs: Define the remodeling work your business accepts and who owns new-project inquiries versus existing-job questions.
Collect the requested scope without presenting it as a verified design or fixed-price package.
Have the office review the summary and confirm a consultation or next action. Any appointment booking must use a supported configuration with the correct appointment type.

sections.title: Set accurate expectations
paragraphs: Intake cannot approve a design, permit, change order, project price or completion date. Do not assume a connection to a remodeling project-management system without verifying the actual workflow.

Revo: current plans and feature boundaries

faqs.q: Can the answering flow collect a project budget?
faqs.a: It can ask an approved question about the caller’s stated budget. That information is not an estimate or a promise the work can be done for that amount.

faqs.q: Can existing customers request scope changes?
faqs.a: They can describe the request. Acceptance and any effect on cost or schedule remain with your authorized team.

faqs.q: Can it book a remodeling consultation?
faqs.a: Only through a supported appointment workflow your office has configured and reviewed. Otherwise capture the preferred next step for staff follow-up.

record.takeaway: Set your answering workflow around the coverage, questions and next steps your business can support.
